compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling emitter writes candidate fixture specs asserting that, for a real plan, a
criterion should fire or stay silent. Those assertions come from history, and history is not
current code. When a candidate disagrees with today's criterion there are two very different
explanations — the candidate is wrong, or the criterion has drifted since the review — and
nothing in the mined data separates them.

Admitting an unverified candidate is worse than having no fixture at all: a wrong must-fire
case encodes a false positive as required behavior and will fail a later, correct rubric
fix. A single confirming run cannot settle it either, because the store holds 551
consecutive review pairs over byte-identical material of which 208 flipped verdict; that is
why every shipped spec uses `epochs: 3` with `gate: at_least(2)`.

## Approach

Run every candidate against current code before admitting it, and keep the disagreements as
evidence rather than discarding a result already paid for.

**Admission run.** For each candidate, execute the criterion's real Pass-1 finder three
times through the existing `calibrate_criterion` path, which issues one
`passes.pass1_chunk` call per case per run scoped to that single criterion
(`eval.py:449-450`, `eval_solver.py:139-142`). A candidate behaving as predicted in at
least two of three runs REPRODUCES. Three runs with a two-of-three threshold is chosen to
match the shipped `at_least(2)` convention rather than inventing a second standard.

**Disposition.** A candidate that reproduces is written to
`.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml`, carrying `blocking` posture when the selector tiered it
as blocking and `advisory` otherwise. A candidate that does not reproduce is withheld from
the suite and written to a drift report recording the criterion, the historical behavior,
the observed current behavior, and the originating review.

**Budget enforcement.** The run pre-flights through `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=250.0)`
using the parameterized ledger from the sibling ledger child, against this epic's own ledger
file, and `finalize()`s priced usage per criterion. Estimate keys are `criteria-eval-cheap`
and `criteria-eval-agent`, selected per criterion from its `exec` tier in
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`. Model parity is pinned to the
production Pass-1 class per ADR 0109.

**Failure disposition.** A criterion is atomic: its spec is written only after all of its
candidates finish their three runs, so a partial criterion never lands. A transient model or
transport error is RETRYABLE and retried within the run. `BudgetExceeded` from the
pre-flight is FATAL and non-retryable — a retry would breach the same ceiling. On a fatal
error the run stops with previously-completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled
into the ledger, so a later re-run resumes at the first uncompleted criterion; when both a
transient failure and the ceiling are in play, the ceiling wins and the run stops.

## Scope

The admission runner, its disposition logic, the drift-report writer, and the
`.rebar/evals/` spec files it produces. Only criteria with no existing spec are written, so
`eval.py:69-78` never resolves a mined file in place of a packaged one.

## Non-goals

- Repairing any drift the report finds; each entry becomes a follow-on ticket linked
  `discovered_from` the parent epic.
- Editing any file under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.
- Re-running admission on a schedule; the sibling self-healing loop owns that.

## Testing

Unit tests drive the disposition logic through a stubbed solver returning scripted fire and
no-fire sequences, so the admit/withhold boundary is deterministic without a model. Separate
unit tests cover the budget refusal against the real `ledger.reserve`, strict validity of
every written spec, and the no-shadowing invariant. One live run against the pinned
production model exercises the real path end to end; it is repeated-trial by construction
(three runs per case) with the two-of-three threshold declared before the run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Against a must-fire candidate, the scripted run sequence (fire, fire, silent) admits it
      and (fire, silent, silent) withholds it and records both behaviors in the drift report;
      verified by `pytest` asserting the written spec contents and the report entry.
- [ ] When the ledger file already holds spend within the ceiling's reserve, the run raises
      `BudgetExceeded` and issues zero model calls; verified by `pytest` asserting the
      exception and a call-counting stub reporting `0`.
- [ ] Every written spec returns zero errors from `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)`;
      verified by `pytest` invoking the real validator over each written file.
- [ ] The set of written filenames shares no member with `ls src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`;
      verified by `pytest` asserting the intersection is empty.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live admission run has completed over the full candidate set with the
      Pass-1 model pinned to its production class, and this epic's ledger records total spend
      greater than zero and at most 250.0 with a per-pass model id on every row.
      provenance: environment=developer workstation against the production Bedrock chain;
      principal=the configured Bedrock identity used by the plan-review gate;
      privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the run must elicit
      real Pass-1 behavior, which no offline analysis can substitute for.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Each drift-report entry has a corresponding ticket linked
      `discovered_from` the parent epic.
      provenance: environment=the rebar tickets store; principal=the session's configured
      rebar assignee; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — ticket
      creation is a store write, not a repository file.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the live admission run has completed; the
drift report and the admitted specs are committed; ledger spend is at most $250.

## Budget

**Hard cap $250**, enforced by `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=250.0)` against this epic's own
ledger file. Central estimate $112 across the uncovered criteria.

file_impact.reason: The reproduce-to-admit runner, its disposition logic and the drift-report writer.
The admitted per-criterion fixture specs this run writes, for criteria that have no existing spec.
The committed record of candidates that failed to reproduce, with historical and observed behavior.
This epic's own append-only budget ledger, separate from the plan-replay ledger.
Unit tests for the admit/withhold boundary under a stubbed solver, the budget refusal, strict spec validity and the no-shadowing invariant.
